summary.text: This CV is a working example, technical product demonstration and open application.
I combine technology and innovation management with strategy and finance.
Evidence: GenAI at CENVION | decision analysis for Swisscom and Airbus.
I also bring M&A, banking and consulting experience. If that fits, let's talk.
To adapt it: target profile | differentiation | two evidenced results | value offered.

lines.text: Some cover letters begin with enthusiasm for a particular vacancy. This one begins deliberately more honestly:
I am looking for a role connecting innovation management and technology with strategy and finance.
ccvl also serves as a product demo of how I structure, measure and rigorously review applications.
At CENVION, I introduced Claude and RAG-based search into investment and reporting workflows.
For seven battery-storage assets, I modelled IRR, NPV, DSCR and sensitivities; the analysis supported
refinancing packages and decisions for institutional investors. I also automated the data flow from
operating data to quarterly reports, making performance gaps and operational improvement levers visible.
That connected emerging technology not to an isolated demonstration, but directly to capital decisions,
risk transparency, portfolio priorities and a more dependable view of operational performance.
At Airbus, I translated 20+ years of safety-critical maintenance data across more than 500 aircraft into
decision-ready risk and cost signals. The work surfaced EUR 100k+ in annual savings potential and helped
trigger an international improvement programme worth more than EUR 1m. At Swisscom, I then modelled
cloud economics and infrastructure choices under data-centre constraints, supported strategic
eight-figure investments and supplier negotiations exceeding CHF 10m for infrastructure programmes.
The recurring pattern is turning technical complexity into evidence specialists and leaders can use together.
This is not a linear specialist profile – and that is precisely where its practical value lies for a team:
I can build a prototype myself, test its technical viability and explain the problem it solves at the same time.
I connect that understanding to the business case, decision risks and the route from an idea into delivery.
Where disciplines otherwise lose momentum at handovers, I join technology, strategy and finance into one
decision base that remains accessible to leaders and credible to the specialists responsible for execution.
For a real application, this is where specific company fit belongs: a strategy, initiative or challenge
that genuinely attracts me – researched and understood rather than praised with interchangeable language.
It then connects that need to my experience and offers a concrete picture of the contribution I could make.
This public version remains deliberately open: if your team wants to implement innovation hands-on and
translate it into commercial decisions, that combination may be worth exploring together.
If you see a possible fit, I would welcome an open conversation about your questions, my experience and
the work where I could genuinely help your team. Thank you for taking the time to consider this unusual
open application – I would be glad to learn more about you, your organisation and the problems ahead.
